# CHANGELOG - Portfolio Project

## [2026-11-14] — The Masthead Ships as WOFF2, the Smoother's Sweep Is Measured at Rest, and the Bar's Empty Middle Becomes a Row of Places

- **One face, one file, one download — the TrueType URL is gone from the critical path** (`index.html` preload `27–34` + `@font-face` `41–60`). `fonts/JSL-Blackletter-Normal.ttf` was **200,152 B** and the face the hero cannot fall back on gracefully, so it was the single largest render-blocking byte on the page. The same outlines are in the repo as **`fonts/JSL-Blackletter-Normal.woff2`, 84,716 B — −58%**, and that is now the only URL in the `src` list: the preload carries `type="font/woff2"` (so a browser that cannot decode it skips the fetch rather than spending it) and `crossorigin` (a font is always fetched CORS-mode, even same-origin — a preload without it is a second download, not a warm cache), and `format('woff2')` is the only format declared. No `truetype` fallback on purpose: every engine that can render this sheet decodes Brotli-compressed WOFF2, so a second URL would only ever be a wasted cache entry. The `.ttf` stays in `fonts/` as the master, **unrequested** — verified by measurement, not by intention: the masthead still sets at **226px** with words **687.83 / 542.13**, identical to the TrueType pass, because `fitName()` measures `scrollWidth` and the two files carry the same advances.
- **`fonts/OldNewspaperTypes.woff2` (36,408 B) and `fonts/The Story of Nothing.woff2` (11,792 B) are staged, not wired.** They are in the repo and referenced by nothing: no preload, no `@font-face`, no `url()` — so they cost the visitor nothing today. Left in place rather than deleted, because the folio line and the colophon are the two places they belong and neither exists yet.
- **`11a.5` now asserts the absence, not just the presence.** The old assertion hard-coded `fonts/JSL-Blackletter-Normal.ttf` / `format('truetype')`, so the faster file could be added without the slower one being removed and the suite would still say yes. It reads the preload (`href` + `type="font/woff2"` + `crossorigin`), the `@font-face` (`src:url('…woff2') format('woff2')` + `font-display:swap`), the token name — **and** that no `url(…ttf` survives anywhere in the stylesheet and no `.ttf` is named in the markup. A WOFF2 that ships beside a TrueType URL is two downloads wearing one claim.
- **The smoother's sweep was a race, and then a stride, and now it is a profile.** `8h.14–16` used to drive the page with four 900px wheels and sleep a fixed 1300 ms; a burst of ~3600px is a Lenis *ease*, not a step, so the sample could land mid-flight at **~2.8k** — a thousand pixels short of the Eid reveal's own start — and read a perfectly correct **0%** that the assertion then scored as a frozen timeline. Three of the five runs that reached the assertion failed that way. Fixing the timer exposed the real number: measured at rest in 900px steps, the reveal reads **0% at 2701px, 12.7575% at 3601px, and the clamped 75% by 4501px** — the window is only ~900px wide, so *any* burst that travels 1800px or more can cross it from 0 to 75 in one step, and an 1800px-stride version did exactly that (one run read **75% at 11,412px twice**, exit 1). The block is now three things: a **resync** (`scrollTo(0)` does not move Lenis's own target, so a 1px wheel makes the smoother adopt the offset the page is actually at before the first burst), **one-wheel steps** with `settledY()` polling until `scrollY` holds still twice running 120 ms apart (a position, not a race), and a **reported pair, not two guesses** — the first rest with a painted circle and a later rest that is both larger and ≥1500px further down, with the whole profile printed in the `A1b` note. Measured on three consecutive runs, byte-identical: `901/0 1801/0 2701/0 3601/12.7575 4501/75 5401/75` → **3601px (12.7575%) → 5401px (75%)**.
- **The bar's empty middle is now a row of places — B1, §05a** (`index.html` landmark + row markup `1639–1682` + `--pop` token `77–82` + §05a styles `256–283` + the tablet band `279–283` + the phone hide `1465–1470` + the three renamed `nav` element selectors `1328` / `1606` / the fixed box `212–215` — 181,598 B / 2,237 lines, SHA-256 `89E8A755…`; harness 857 → **869 assertions**). Workstream B left the bar as "a place, not a menu": a breadcrumb on the left, a gear on the right, and **nothing in between** — a 1440px bar with one 190px label and one 19px handle, which read as unfinished rather than as restraint. The head now prints the page's four sections in that space, and the reason it is not a fifth list is that it is **the same list**: the same four `#who`/`#work`/`#magazine`/`#reach` hrefs, the same `01 / 02 / ∗ / 03` numerals and the same four names the contents strip prints under the sheet, and the same `data-nav-for` attribute the breadcrumb's rows carry — so `main.js`'s existing single loop over `rows` writes `aria-current` onto the strip's row **and** the bar's link in one pass and the two surfaces cannot disagree about where the visitor is (`9i.10`).
  - **The landmark and the box are two different jobs, so they are two different elements.** `<header class="site-head">` is the landmark and the fixed box (`position:fixed` + `z-index:510`, the rule `11a.14` already looked for); `#siteNav.head-bar` is the row inside it that every measurement and every scroll write already targets — `nav-hidden`'s `translateY(-101%)`, the padding that keeps it on `--gutter`, the background pseudo-element. The wrapper is `pointer-events:none` and the row is `pointer-events:auto`, so the fixed header's empty corners cannot eat a press meant for the sheet underneath. That is why the rename was a straight swap of three selectors (`nav{padding…}` → `.head-bar{…}` at `1328`, `nav.nav-hidden{…}` → `.head-bar.nav-hidden{…}`, `nav,.set-drawer{transition:none!important}` → `.head-bar,.set-drawer`) with no geometry moving: measured at every audited width, the bar still sits on `--gutter` to within 0.6px (`8c`).
  - **Four inks, zero new colours.** Each link carries one inline `--pop`, and every value is already on the sheet — `var(--accent)` oxblood for who (`#7A1818`), the riso rose `#C06060` that work's log and reach's heading use, `var(--brass)` `#9E7428`, and `var(--bone)` `#EDE6D4` for reach's dark field — with `--pop:var(--brass)` at `:root` so the token always resolves and a link that set no inline still fills with something belonging to the sheet. Resolved live at 1440 the four compute to exactly those four values (`9i.9`), every one distinct. Hover and `aria-current` fill the square with it, which is the point: the current section is the colour of the section itself. The square is **drawn** (0.5rem box + hairline that fills), not typed — a `▪` glyph changes size and baseline with every face in the fallback stack, and the row sits next to a blackletter name.
  - **At 537px it is a row; at 834 it is numerals; at 390 it is not drawn.** Measured: **537px wide starting at x 771** at 1440 (`9i.7`/`9i.8`), inside the bar and clear of both the breadcrumb's right edge and the gear's left. Between 768 and 1024 the labels come out and only squares and numerals remain, the row is left to shrink (`min-width:0`) rather than given `width:100%` — a 100% item in this `space-between` flex row would bid against the gear's own box — and the band is measured, not assumed: at **834** the bar is one line, no overflow, and the gear still hit-tests at its centre (`9i.12`). Below 768 the row is `display:none` (`9i.5`/`9i.6`): the strip under the sheet already prints these four names on a phone and the breadcrumb's list already holds them as 44px rows, so a third copy would only spend a 390px bar on targets too small to hit.
  - **A jump to the magazine lights both surfaces.** `9i.10` scrolls 500px into `#magazine` and reads `aria-current="location"` on **2 of 2** of that section's `[data-nav-for]` nodes with **0** stale elsewhere while the bar's own label agrees ("Akcidental Vision"); `9i.11` then confirms the lit square's computed background is `rgb(158, 116, 40)` — the brass its inline `--pop` names.
- **Verification.** `node verify.mjs` → **869 assertions, 869 passing, exit 0** on three consecutive runs, the head-row note byte-identical each time (`1440 537px wide at x 771, inks #7A1818/#C06060/#9E7428/#EDE6D4`). Nothing is known to fail.

## [2026-11-14] — The Hero Becomes a Gothic Riso Broadsheet: Blackletter, Vinyl and Three Drums

- **The sheet, reprinted as a broadsheet — §06 rebuilt end to end** (`index.html` §06 `330–486` + §06b `488–512` + the sheet's media blocks at `1092–1121` / `1198–1201` / `1264–1268` / `1447–1449` + the two off-switch blocks `1497–1500` / `1514–1519` / `1529` / `1545` + the sprite's second filter `1642–1655` + the hero markup `1657–1724` + the strip's rows `1736–1759` + the Draggable script `2140–2146` — 162,849 → **175,230 B / 2,030 → 2,171 lines**, LF-only, BOM-free, SHA-256 `AC139413…`; `js/main.js` 128,204 → **140,641 B / 2,211 → 2,410 lines**, `57BAC5CF…` — the smoother's velocity callback `110–121`, the hero module `301–603`, the retired plate / clock / `is-scrolled` writers `605–614` / `611–614` / `2050–2065` / `2164–2165`; new `js/Draggable.min.js` **35,762 B**, `EB28FF7A…`, vendored rather than CDN-pinned; new `fonts/JSL-Blackletter-Normal.ttf` **200,152 B**, `BA10BB54…`; two new plates `images/sticker-aliasgar.png` **316,912 B / 2000×2000**, `73B893C7…`, and `images/sticker-dalal.png` **270,763 B / 1918×657**, `BAD25E3E…`; `js/lenis.min.js` untouched at 18,392 B / `239B9506…`; **`js/ledger.js` is outside this workstream and unchanged** — 20,146 B / 407 lines / `6AE82DBA…`, so the register work in flight stays with its own entry; harness 837 → **857 assertions, 857 passing**, exit 0, nothing known to fail)
  - **The palette is scoped to the sheet, and that is the whole reason it works.** `--paper:#EAE7E0` and `--ink:#141110` are declared **on `#hero`**, not on `:root`, because `:root`'s `--ink` is the navy chrome token that `.wall-room` and `#cur.cur-ink` already consume — rewriting it globally would have repainted the nav and the rail a warm near-black. Scoped, the sheet is newsprint while the contents strip *below* it (which is outside `#hero`) keeps the night ink, and the seam between them is the strip itself. `isolation:isolate` stays load-bearing: the three riso drums multiply against this stock and never through it to the bone page behind. The crop marks and the registration crosshair were re-inked from `--muted-dark` (a bone token, invisible on paper) to `--rule-ink`.
  - **One screen minus the strip, stated once.** The hero's height and the strip's height were two numbers that had to agree — `100vh` in one rule and a measured `44.19px` in another — so they are now one token: `--marquee-h:2.6rem` (44.2px at the 106.25% root) and `#hero{min-height:calc(100svh - var(--marquee-h))}`, with a hard `height:calc(100vh - var(--marquee-h))` from 1200 up. Measured: sheet **855.8** at 900, strip **44.19**, the strip's top landing on the sheet's bottom to a hundredth — so the dock is a fold, not an approximation. At 768 the sheet is **890.53 of 900** and at 390 **799.8 of 844**: the lock is a floor, and a phone's content is allowed to be taller than it.
  - **The masthead is one face at one size.** JSL Blackletter is preloaded **with `crossorigin`** (a font is always fetched in CORS mode, so a preload without it is a second download, not a warm cache) and swapped in; `fitName()` now shrinks BOTH rows together until the wider one fits, because the 0.62 second-line factor was compensating for an italic Cormorant cut that no longer exists. It measures `scrollWidth`, not a rect: each word rides in a shrink-to-fit `.sticker-group`, and a rect reports "it fits" for a word that is overflowing its capped box. The second row is `DALAL` in the source rendered as **small caps** — the first letter keeps full cap height, the rest sit at x-height — which is the broadsheet convention and the only way a blackletter reads as one word. Measured at 1440: **226px**, words **687.83 / 542.13**, both inside the 691px stage.
  - **Two real vinyl plates, and they are percentages OF THEIR WORDS.** `.sticker-group` is an inline-block, so its width *is* the word's width at every viewport and in both faces; `width:46%` is 46% of the letters, with no JavaScript measurement and nothing to drift when the face lands (the 1918×657 dalal plate gets its own `aspect-ratio`, because forcing a wide die-cut into a square would letterbox it to a third of its width). **Two nodes, because two transforms cannot share one:** `.sticker-slot` carries the scroll parallax (speed 1.5) and the `.sticker` inside it carries the hand — Draggable owns x/y, GSAP owns the jitter (±16px, ±4° around a −5° rest angle, re-rolled per load) and the velocity skew. The **shadow is a silhouette, not a box**: the first cut painted a rounded rectangle, and on a die-cut with transparent corners that reads as a grey card, so the layer is a second copy of the same image (same URL — no second download) blurred and darkened, and the shadow takes the sticker's own outline. The **gloss** writes `--bubble-x/--bubble-y` and never a transform, because the transform belongs to GSAP and a second writer there would fight the drag. `touch-action:none` is scoped to the sticker so the sheet keeps `pan-y` and a thumb anywhere else still scrolls the page. The stickers are `<button tabindex="-1" aria-hidden>`: there is no keyboard equivalent of "move this 40px left", and a control that announces itself and then does nothing is a worse lie than decoration.

  - **Two saturated multiplies can only end at black — so the drums are LIGHT.** A real riso drum lays a tint, not a coat: the colour plates are flattened toward a light ink (`saturate(3.4)`, `brightness(1.2)`, `contrast(0.72)`) and the KEY is the only plate that goes to black (`contrast(1.62) brightness(0.62)`) — which is why the overprint reads as a third colour instead of a hole. The **filter sits on each layer, never on the stack**: a `filter` on the parent makes it an isolated group, so every child's `multiply` would blend against transparency instead of paper and the key would simply cover the colours. Per-layer also buys per-drum misregistration, which is how a press actually slips. `url(#riso-ink-bleed)` is feTurbulence (low frequency, four octaves — a high frequency reads as sandpaper) plus a 2.4px feDisplacementMap, and its region is **x −18% / width 136%** because the displacement samples outside the box and the default −10%/120% cuts it into a hard band exactly where the bleed must not be.
  - **One frame for the sheet, and it keeps running until the flick is done.** The smoother's velocity is read through a single `smoothLenis.on('scroll')` attached where the instance is built (a rebuild re-attaches it exactly once — `destroy()` takes it with the instance) and falls back to a frame delta where Lenis deliberately does not exist, below 768. That velocity is damped into **±2.2° of skewY** on the masthead, the plate and the stickers plus a hair of scaleY, and the loop **re-arms itself while `|v| > 0.0015`** — without that line the last flick's lean would be the state the sheet kept until the next scroll event, and a page that stopped dead would stay leaning. Four parallax speeds read the same position (`0.8` stock, `1.0` masthead, `1.2` plate, `1.5` stickers ⇒ at y 300: **+60 / 0 / −60 / −150**), and the gear turns **252.6°** through that third of the sheet. Measured peak lean: **1.64°**.
  - **The harness grew a second opinion about every one of those claims.** `verify.mjs`'s `STEP 11a` was rewritten (16 source assertions: scoped palette, `--marquee-h`, the preload's `crossorigin`, `@font-face`, small caps, the three drums and their order, the ink-bleed filter's region, the two buttons and their three layers, the vendored Draggable's position **before** `main.js`, the four-name strip, and both off-switch blocks naming the four inline-transform writers), `11b/11c` re-derive the geometry from the new selectors and the 44px the sheet lost, `11e` now measures **drift and shuffle** instead of depth (edge → **7.81 / −6.08 / 0 px**: the two colour drums opposite, the key dead still), and `11k/11l/11m` are new — the transient skew, the four depths and the gear, and a real press-drag-release with its gloss. Three traps were worth the ink: **(1)** a sticky element's `rect.top` clamps at 0 once it is stuck, so "halfway through the handoff" has to be measured from the strip's **document** top, not `900 − h/2`; **(2)** `skewY` is a shear — it lands in the matrix's `c`/`d` and leaves `a`/`b` untouched, so `atan2(b,a)` measures exactly nothing of it and the skew has to be read back from **GSAP's own cache**; **(3)** the `Aliasgar` sticker reaches into the plate's left half at 1440 with `z-index:6`, so the first pointer probe aimed at the plate's edge was landing on vinyl — the probe moved to the outer edge, and the gloss probe now **samples the visible box with `elementFromPoint`** instead of trusting a rotated rect. The static server also learned `'.ttf': 'font/ttf'`, without which Chrome refuses the face with a MIME warning and the no-console-error gate fails on a file that is perfectly fine.
  - **Retired, and the source says so.** The slug (`#heroClock`, the coordinates, `Plate 00`), the display asterisk (`#heroAsterisk`), the accent hairline, the tagline, the four dust specks, the halftone and accent passes, the plate's pointer parallax and the `B1 Personal archive` row in the contents strip are all gone; `html.is-scrolled` went with the one rule that read it, so `ASTERISK_AT` and its class write are gone from the bar's frame rather than left as a selector nothing can match. `9a.7` and `9b` were inverted to assert the retirement (no element, no lookup, no write, and no class invented 260px down), `11a.15` counts **eight rows / four focusable** in the strip while the archive door stays in the bar, and `11g.5` follows at **8 / 4**. The one thing that is *not* retired: the plate's old parallax is now the riso drift, and it writes through GSAP — the raw `style.transform` it used to write was the bug this rebuild could not afford, because GSAP's cache does not know about a matrix written behind its back.

## [2026-11-11] — The Hero Becomes a Press Sheet: Four Crop Marks, Three Passes and One Handoff

- **The Sheet, the Plate and the Signboard — the hero rebuilt as a printed page** (`index.html` §06 305–409 + new §06b 411–432 + the sheet's media blocks at 1031 / 1133 / 1190–1200 / 1379–1386 / 1429–1432 / 1439 / 1456–1458 / 1469 + markup 1567–1643 — 144,519 → **162,849 B / 1,819 → 2,030 lines**, LF-only, BOM-free, SHA-256 `E067502C…`; `js/main.js` 114,411 → **128,204 B / 1,979 → 2,211 lines**, `C2BA3A6B…` — the name reveal 324–377, the plate 379–417, the clock 419–449, the handoff inside the bar's frame at 1805–1816 / 1894–1897 / 1906–1915 / 2028–2048; `js/lenis.min.js` untouched at 18,392 B / `239B9506…`; **`js/ledger.js` is outside this workstream and unchanged** — 20,146 B / 407 lines / `6AE82DBA…`, so the register work in flight stays with its own entry; one new plate `images/hero-photo-new.png` at 314,699 B / 699×532 RGBA, fetched once and inked three ways; harness 768 → **837 assertions, 837 passing**, exit 0, nothing known to fail)
  - **Nothing on the sheet is an image asset.** The paper is one SVG filter — `feTurbulence` at three octaves, generated at the element's own size, so a 2560px hero never shows a 280px repeat — lain over the ink field at 50%. The four crop marks are Ls cut from two 1px edges, 13px each, sat on the sheet's own `--hero-pad`: markup a printer would recognise, with nothing drawn between them. The registration crosshair is an inline 32px SVG, one request lighter than a texture and free to take the sheet's ink colour. Four dust specks. And the asterisk that left the chrome in §05 lives here now, at display size, `aria-hidden`, gone over the first 50px of scroll. `isolation:isolate` is load-bearing rather than tidy: the plate's `multiply` and `color` passes have to blend with the sheet and never through it to the bone page behind — and `overflow:hidden` is what lets the plate reach into the outer track without that bleed becoming a scrollbar. The one bug worth the ink: the first cut of the crosshair styled `.reg-crosshair svg`, matched nothing — the svg **is** the element carrying the class — and the browser's default black fill duly painted a solid disc where a crosshair belongs. The paint sits on the element itself now.
  - **At 1200 and up the hero stands in the same grid every other band stands in.** `grid-template-columns:var(--frame-cols)` at zero padding, so the sheet's left edge **is** the frame's left edge; the portrait names `grid-column:2/4` and bleeds into the outer track, and a track resolves against the client box — scrollbar-exact, no `100vw` anywhere. Both children name **row 1** as well as their columns: auto-placement would see the plate overlapping `.hero-left`'s track, give it a row of its own, and a second row would split the sheet in two. Measured: **1200 → 60 / 1065 / 60, plate 504×720 at x 681→1185, sheet 900 tall**; **1440 → 72.5 / 1280 / 72.5, plate 604.8×720 at x 820.2→1425**; **2560 → 632.5 / 1280 / 632.5, plate 620×720 at x 1925→2545**. The plate stops at 2545 rather than 2560 because it lives inside the frame's right gutter, and the sheet is exactly `100vh` with `min-height:0` — which is what makes the contents strip's dock land on the fold rather than near it. Below 1200 none of that applies. 768–800 is a tablet's band and the plate is sized by **height** (`clamp(280px,36vh,420px)`, width from its own 699:532), so a wide column never lets an absolute plate dictate the page; the phone is sized by **width** (`min(86vw,48vh)`), so `scrollWidth` cannot pass the gutter — measured **768 → sheet 828 of 900, plate 425.7×324 at x 327.3, slug ends 423.39 < 701.61**; **390 → sheet 776.47 of 844, plate 335.39×255.25 at x 39.61, slug 222.33 < 336.5**.
  - **One plate, printed in three passes.** Three `<img>` elements point at the same file, so the browser fetches 314 KB once: the **base** is the photograph in monochrome (`grayscale(1) contrast(1.06) brightness(0.9)`); the **halftone** is its screen — a 5px radial-gradient mask (1.05px dot, 1.6px clear) multiplied down at 72% and warmed toward the brass, so the mid-tones read as a printed tint instead of a dark photograph; the **accent** is the third ink — the plate recoloured to the accent and blended in `color`, so the figure keeps its own luminosity and borrows the sheet's one hue, under a 104° gradient mask that makes it a plate wipe and not a red photograph. The cutout keeps its own alpha, so no pass needs the silhouette as a mask, and no pass takes a pointer. `width`/`height` are the file's own 699×532 and `object-position:right bottom` holds the figure on the sheet's corner at every width — which is also why the plate is reserved before its bytes land and the sheet never jumps under its own reveal.
  - **The parallax is depth, not decoration.** The pointer's offset from the plate's centre, normalised against `max(240, w/2)` and clamped to −1..1, translates the three passes by 5 / 11 / 18px at full deflection: a stack of printed layers, ratios 2.2 and 3.6. It is **one rAF loop that stops when it has caught up** (0.002 of a step, ~0.1 lerp), so a static hero is not a permanent frame loop; it never reads a rect inside the loop — the rect is read on the event — and it parks at zero for a coarse pointer (no hover to read) and for Motion off, which is written by a `MutationObserver` on `data-motion`, so the drawer's switch never has to know this module exists. Measured with the reticle at the plate's edge: **−4.71 / −10.36 / −16.95px**; at its centre: **0.12 / 0.27 / 0.45px**.
  - **The name arrives from behind a mask that does not cut its own ascenders.** `.hero-line` clips with `clip-path:inset(-25% -12% 0 -12%)` rather than `overflow:hidden`: the reveal slides each line up from below, so the only hard edge it needs is the bottom one, and clipping a 0.865 line box at the top would shave the cap off a 140px display face. The character-by-character intro is gone with its `innerHTML` rewrite — the `h1` keeps its own text node — and the two lines are children of masks that are already `translateY(110%)` for the tween to move to 0 (1.4s `expo.out`, 0.15s stagger). That tween needed `y:0` written beside `yPercent:0`: GSAP caches the element's CSS transform as `y` in px, so animating the percentage alone finished exactly where it started — the bug that looks like *the reveal never ran*. No GSAP, or no motion, is not a degraded hero: the same `transform:none` the tween ends on is written in one frame, and the stylesheet says so twice (`[data-motion="off"]` and `prefers-reduced-motion`).
  - **The slug carries the sheet's own clock.** Coordinates, plate number and a running Gulf time, set as a printer's slug at the foot of the page: `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB', …, timeZone:'Asia/Dubai')` with a local-time fallback for a browser without IANA zones, at most one text node per second, stopped for a hidden tab and for Motion off — measured **23:28:43 → 23:28:44, Gulf 23:28:44, 0s apart**. It is `aria-hidden`, because a running second is a detail of the object and not information a reader needs. On a ≤520px phone the first field goes instead of the line: the coordinates measured **410px against a 375px viewport**, and dropping them lets the clock and the plate number still fit beside a 4px dot without the ticker running past the sheet's right crop mark — the paragraph above the fold still says where the work was made.
  - **The signboard is the bar's entrance, and the two are exact complements.** The five names the bar gave up in §05 are now a sticky contents strip: 2.6rem of ink at z 500 (the bar sits at 510, one above it, because the bar is what the strip becomes), two identical lists so the −50% loop has a seam with no script and no gap — the second `aria-hidden` with `tabindex=-1` on its links, so a screen reader and the Tab ring hear the contents exactly once. It runs at 46s linear, pauses on hover and on `focus-within` (a moving target is not a click target), and stops dead under Motion off. The handoff is **one measurement written twice**: `dock` is how far the strip has risen through its own height, the bar's opacity **is** that number and the strip's type is its inverse, written as per-frame values rather than transitions, which would lag the wheel by their own duration. Measured **y 0 → 0 / 1**, **y 878 → 0.502 / 0.498**, **y 1400 → 1 / 0** — one surface at the top at every position, and the two always sum to 1. Three things outrank the fade and hold the bar at 1: its own list open, focus inside it (`:focus-visible`, deferred one task so "moved to another control" is not read as "left"), and the drawer open, whose gear lives in the bar. The start state is written in the parse (`opacity:0` before the first frame), so a page that opens on the hero never flashes a bar it is about to hide.
  - **Nothing that draws anything else moved.** The who-photo is still `images/hero-photo.png` and its clip is still on `view()`; §02's A2/A3 layout hand-tuning is still deferred and still untouched; the rail, the breadcrumb, the list and the drawer measure exactly as they did, and their chapters' assertions still pass. Motion off is not a broken sheet but a still one: the plate's reveal lands in one frame, the lines sit at `transform:none`, the strip is a printed row of names, the clock stops, and the file's `prefers-reduced-motion` block says the same in CSS. The harness grew by ten steps — 11a–11j, from the source through three widths of sheet geometry, two narrow widths, the mask, the three passes, the clock, the handoff and the reticle's top-layer move — and is **837 assertions, exit 0, nothing known to fail**.

  - **`--onpage-cap` is one number, declared once, next to the same doctrine `--art-cap` already follows.** `#work` declares `--onpage-cap:56vh` (`56dvh` behind `@supports (height:1dvh)`) and each card derives its **width**: `--lf-card-w:min(var(--lf-thumb-w), calc(var(--onpage-cap) * var(--lf-ratio)))` on `.leaflet-thumb` (`--lf-thumb-w:30rem`, `--lf-ratio:0.7066`), `--dyk-w:min(100%, 480px, calc(var(--onpage-cap) * var(--dyk-ratio)))` on `.case-04` (`--dyk-ratio:0.703`). Measured after: **356.1 × 504** @1440×900, **303.9 × 430.1** @1440×768 and @1024×768, **334 × 472.6** @390×844, **154.3 × 218.4** @844×390 — every one exactly `56dvh` tall, ratio **0.7066** at all five.
  - **The labels are now as wide as the image they name.** `.comparison` and `.dyk-labels` each carried their own `max-width:480px`, so the "What I designed / What shipped" pair could sit wider than the slider under it, and both kept the old measure when the image shrank. They now share `--dyk-w`: **354.3 × 504** @1440×900, **302.3 × 430.1** @1440×768, **332.3 × 472.6** @390×844, with `labels` and `image` reporting the same width and the same left edge to the tenth of a pixel. Nothing inside the slider changed — the divider, the handle, the `clip-path` inset `main.js` writes are all percentage- or rect-based, so the cap never reached them.
  - **The wall had two layouts pretending to be one: a fixed right-hand label track and a work that had to be pushed right to reach it.** The grid gave every row the same tracks, so the bingo (2.5:1, the only work that fills its column) looked correct and the 4:5 portrait did not: `margin-left:auto` hung it against the placard, measured **463.3 → 952.9**, leaving a 320px hole on its left and its own caption 57.6px from an edge it did not reach. `.art-wall` is a `flex-direction:column` stack of `.art-work` rows now, each row `display:flex;align-items:flex-end`, the frame `flex:1 1 0` and the placard `flex:0 1 13.5rem;min-width:10.5rem` — the same `minmax(10.5rem,13.5rem)` track, so the bingo's arithmetic is the old grid's to the pixel (**1040 − 229.5 − 57.6 = 752.9**) while the leftover now falls to the right of every work instead of in front of one. Measured: the bingo is byte-identical at all five viewports (**753×301 @200**, **651×260 @51**, **496×199 @42**, **351×140 @20**), and the portrait is **489.6×612 @200 → 689.6** with its label at **747.2** instead of **1010.5** — a 263px move for the caption, a 57.6px gap preserved on both rows (41px at 1024, 33.8px at 844). `max-height:var(--art-cap)` + `overflow:clip` are a belt on the same braces: never fires while a work's `--art-ratio` is honest (frame height == image height), and clips neither the inset hairline ring nor the hover lift. Below 800px the row becomes a column and the frame takes `flex:none` — load-bearing, because `flex:1 1 0` on the block axis collapses the work's height to 0, and the stacked wall still measures **351×140** and **351×439** at 390×844 with its caption spanning the column.
  - **A card can be capped and still not fit, so the chrome gave some air back.** With the untightened spacing the budget at 1440×768 was **52.2vh**, which no card worth looking at can live inside. A `@media (max-height:940px)` block returns **42.5px above** the card (case padding 4.5rem → 3rem, title margin 3rem → 2rem) and **12.75px below** it (stage margin 2rem → 1.25rem; the comparison's 2.5rem → 1.5rem, hint 2rem → 1.25rem), lifting that budget to **59.4vh** — and the other four to 65.4 / 61.6 / 65.9 / 26.1vh. **56vh** is the number that leaves **26px** of slack at the tightest laptop; **58vh** also fits at 1440×768 but with 11px, which is not a margin, it is a coincidence waiting for a font metric. Measured, the CTA and the hint now end at **816 / 814** of 900, **742 / 741** of 768, **725 / 724** of 768 and **761 / 794** of 844 — inside the screen in every case, with the title above them and nothing under the rail.
  - **A phone held sideways cannot hold the intro, and the suite says so instead of pretending.** At 844×390 the room under the rail is **329px**; the case head plus a *capped* 218px card is already 378px, so "title + card + CTA on one screen" is unachievable there at any cap that leaves a recognisable card. The assertion is tiered exactly on that arithmetic: on any viewport ≥ 720px tall the whole intro must fit (title ≥ rail, CTA/hint ≤ the fold); everywhere, the card and its CTA must share one screen once the *card's* top is under the rail — **571 / 497 / 497 / 540 / 286px** against rooms of 839 / 707 / 707 / 783 / 329. That last one caught the first draft of this change, which asserted from the *case's* top and failed at 844×390 by 116px.
  - **The suite described the grid, so the three probes that read it were rewritten.** `.art-work`'s `gridTemplateColumns` was load-bearing in two stacking checks and in STEP 6's `col` measurement; both stacking checks now read `flexDirection` (so they still bite instead of comparing the string `none`), and `col` subtracts the work's **own** label (`wr.width − label.width − gap`) rather than a trailing track — the bingo still reports **753 of 753** and the portrait **418 of 418** at 1024. STEP 6's label check moved from `r.w <= 800 ||` to `labelW < 1 ||`, so it now skips only a genuinely hidden placard, and gained `hungLeft` (both works' left edges within 1px). The morph assertion `fly[0] > panel[0]` became `>= panel[0] * 0.9`: a capped card may legitimately be a hair narrower than a panel, and the ratio check is what actually guarantees no smear. STEP 7 is new — **24 assertions** across the five viewports (budget, derived-not-declared, card+CTA, the ≥720px full-intro tier, labels = image) plus three screenshots at 1440×768 and 1440×900, and the run's watchdog went 300s → 420s to hold them.
  - **What did not change: the JavaScript, the tilt, the morph, and the mobile stack.** `js/main.js` is byte-identical (**85,952 B**, `96521AA2…`) — the tilt reads `getBoundingClientRect()`, the Flip inverts a rect, the wall toggles a class, and all three are size-agnostic. `MAX_TILT` 6°, the `--gx/--gy` sheen, the `pointer:fine` and reduced-motion gates, and the 1.46× perspective (`calc(var(--lf-card-w) * 1.46)` — 520px where the cap bites, 744.6px at full size) still pass their round-trip assertions, the fly layer still starts on the thumbnail's exact rect, and the stacked wall still reveals its caption on a tap. The 24 new checks and the 6 pre-existing STEP 3b audio failures are the whole of the delta: **187/193 → 211/217**.
## [2026-10-20]
- **The Wall Fits the Room, the Gutter Holds Still, and the Press Follows the Mark** (`index.html` §04 reticle `pointer-events` + §05 nav mark + §06 wall geometry and rail + §13 stacked layout + §12 markup — 94,633 B / 1,201 lines, LF-only, BOM-free, SHA-256 `DBBA91A8…`; `js/main.js` §01 lock + §03 reticle router — 85,952 B / 1,502 lines, `96521AA2…`; harness 177 → 193 checks, the six pre-existing STEP 3b audio assertions still the only failures)
  - **`width:100%` sized the frame from the column, so `object-fit` could never have saved it.** At 1440 the art track is **752.9 px**; a 4:5 portrait in it is **941 px** tall against an **828 px** visible budget — 113 px of scroll before the 72 px rail and the section padding are counted. `object-fit:contain` on that box would have letterboxed the shadow and the hairline hover ring around 130 px of air, so the box itself had to shrink: `.art-wall` now declares one number, `--art-cap:68vh` (`68dvh` behind `@supports (height:1dvh)`), and `.art-frame` derives its width as `min(100%, calc(var(--art-cap) * var(--art-ratio,1)))`. Each `<figure>` declares its own `--art-ratio` from the asset (**2.5** = 1500×600, **0.8** = 1500×1875); the fallback is a deliberate square, so a work that forgets its ratio is visibly wrong and fails the suite instead of borrowing another's shape. `margin-left:auto` hangs the work against the placard on desktop, `margin-inline:auto` centres it in the stacked layout below 800 px.
  - **Measured, one work per screen, vertical overflow 0 px at every size** (frame w×h): **753×301 + 490×612** @1440×900 (was 753×301 + **753×941**), **753×301 + 418×522** @1440×768, **651×260 + 418×522** @1024×768, **496×199 + 212×265** @844×390, **351×140 + 351×439** @390×844. The 2.5:1 bingo is unchanged at every width because `min()` resolves to 100% — 612 × 2.5 > 752.9 — which is why the wall still reads as the same wall. Scrolled to the rail (`scroll-padding-top:5rem`), the portrait's bottom lands at **714 / 624 / 624 / 367 / 541** of 900/768/768/390/844.
  - **`height:auto` is the other half of the `width`/`height` attributes, and it cost a round trip.** Reserving the box before the bytes land also pins `height:1875px`: an attribute is a presentational hint, and `.art-img{width:100%}` only overrides the axis it names. The wall measured **1977 px tall at all five viewports** until `.art-img,.who-portrait-img` carried `height:auto`. Caught by the ratio assertion (418/1875 = **0.223** against 0.800), not by the eye — it reads as "the portrait is a bit tall".
  - **The asterisk was a 37.6 px target behind a 30 px magnet.** `#cur` was already `pointer-events:none` — nothing was swallowing the press. `cursor:none` hides the system pointer, the magnet pulls the mark onto the glyph from up to 104 px away, and the click is still dispatched at the pointer, so aiming with the mark put the press outside a hit box that measured **37.6 × 44.2 px**: the asterisk "sometimes" did nothing because the visitor was aiming correctly and hitting correctly. Two mechanical changes: `.nav-mark::after{inset:-1rem}` widens the target to **45.0 × 51.5 px on a 0.5 px scan (44.4 × 51.0 by arithmetic, inset −17 px at the 17 px root)**, clearing the 44 px minimum on the axis a visitor actually aims at; and a capture-phase router delivers the press to `elementFromPoint(cx, cy)` — what the mark is over — when the pointer missed it. The magnet is untouched: the mark still snaps **0.7 px** from the glyph centre, a press 30 px away now opens the wall, sets `aria-expanded="true"`, and lands focus on `#artClose`.
  - **The router cannot become a ghost click or a hijack.** It returns early on `e.detail === 0` (keyboard, and its own synthetic press, so it cannot loop), on `!tracking`, on a mark that is off (`cur-on`) or hidden (the magnifier state), and on a pointer that already hit the target. `locked.el` only ever holds an anchor that passed the visibility hit test in the frame loop, so a control behind the open wall can never be activated this way, and the element under the pointer never fires alongside. Asserted three ways: hidden mark → wall stays shut; pointer 300 px away → mark is not on the glyph and the press does nothing; keyboard activation still works with the handler in place.
  - **Locking the body moved the page ~15 px, and measuring the gutter is what stops it.** `overflow:hidden` removes the classic scrollbar, the viewport widens, and every fixed element plus the centred column slides right for as long as an overlay is open. `syncScrollLock()` now measures the gutter around the lock — `innerWidth − clientWidth` before, minus the same reading after — pads `<body>` by it, and publishes it as `--sbw` for the two fixed rails (`nav`, `.art-nav`), which sit outside the body box and cannot be padded with it. Two readings of 0 (overlay scrollbars, or a platform that reserves the gutter itself) mean nothing is padded at all. `data-scroll-lock` makes it idempotent, so a `pageshow` or `visibilitychange` re-sync cannot double-pad, and the unlock clears padding, `--sbw` and the attribute even if a previous open died mid-flight. Measured with scrollbars forced back on (they are hidden for the rest of the run): `clientWidth 1440 → 1440 → 1440`, `.nav-links` right edge `1368.0 → 1368.0 → 1368.0`, `--sbw` gone after close.
  - **Tab now clears the sticky rail.** `.art-overlay{scroll-padding-top:5rem}` and `.art-work{scroll-margin-top:1rem}`: before this, focusing the second work scrolled it under the 72 px rail.
  - **Sixteen new harness checks, and the one that fails on the old tree is the point.** Five budget assertions (68vh per work, frame ratio against the asset's own pixels ±0.006, the 2.5:1 column unchanged, the placard gap, shadow on the art and not on air, `overflowX = 0`), five "scrolled to the rail it still ends on screen", the declared-budget check, the hit box, the gutter, and three routing cases. **G6 — the press 30 px off the glyph — is the reproduction of the report**, and it fails before the patch by construction, because the press never reached the asterisk. The stacked-layout probe had to learn that a one-track grid has no placard column to subtract. Remaining failures: the six pre-existing STEP 3b audio assertions, unchanged in count and identity — four are that block pressing `#footerEgg` from `window.scrollTo(0,0)`, where the footer asterisk sits far below the fold and the press lands on nothing, and two are leaflet flap probes run while the sheet is face-down. None of the six touches the wall's geometry or its input path.
  - **Left alone on purpose.** `.art-nav-label` is a decorative asterisk that looks like a control; it is `aria-hidden` and always was, so it stays a mark rather than being promoted to a fourth door. The page behind an open overlay is still not `inert` — the wall's `clip-path` plus `pointer-events` already keeps the press out, and the hide-on-close path is covered by the Tab-ring assertion.
- **The Leaflet Is One Sheet on Three Hinges, and the Shadows Went Back onto the Table** (`index.html` §09 leaflet CSS 329–393 + the modal markup + §13 responsive — 87,642 → 91,945 B / 1,118 → 1,172 lines, LF-only, BOM-free, SHA-256 `F537C51F…`; `js/main.js` 463–776 — 78,075 → 83,070 B / 1,361 → 1,460 lines, `B7EFFE13…`; GSAP 3.15.0 + Flip 3.15.0 from cdnjs, SRI-pinned; harness 87/87 new)
  - **Four flaps in two spreads became four panels on three hinges.** The old object was two static pages with a 100° flap hinged over each, plus a second spread parked at 180° for the products: four pieces of paper that happened to overlap, with the fold looked after by two independent damped springs. It is now a chain — `hinge += u·cos θ`, `depth -= u·sin θ` — so leaf 0's spine is the only fixed point, leaf 1 lands on the hinge leaf 0 handed it, and the folded footprint is exactly one panel (`[0,180,0,180]`) against the open one of exactly four (`[0,0,0,0]`). `c` releases the strip separately: 1.5u centres the stack inside the four-panel box, 0 centres the open sheet, and tweening it is what makes the sheet look placed down rather than dragged open. Measured with the camera neutralised: hinges at **0 / 270 / 540 / 810 px** and every panel **270.00 px** at 1440 and 1920; **220.16 px** at 1024 (strip 880.91 against 4u of 880.63, **0.28 px**); the folded stack at **405.0 px = 1.5 × 270.0** at every desktop width; horizontal overflow **0 px** on the document and on the dialog at all five viewports.
  - **One writer, and no CSS spring left to disagree with it.** `S{th[], c, camX, camY, camZ, yaw}` is tweened — by GSAP when it is on the wire, by assignment when it is not — and a single `render()` composes every leaf transform plus the rig's camera. Nothing else may write a leaf matrix, which is why the old `.lf-book-container{transform:translateY(12px) scale(0.972)}` spring with its 0.9 s transition is gone, and why the modal's own `opacity` fade moved to a `.lf-room` sibling: an `opacity` on an ancestor flattens a `preserve-3d` subtree, and the chain needs `preserve-3d` on the rig, the accordion and all four leaves (verified on 12 nodes: `transform-style` preserved, no `filter`, no `box-shadow`). The camera sits one level *above* the chain — perspective and transform on `.lf-rig`, pure hinge maths inside it — so a leaf never has to know where the viewer is.
  - **Flip carries the cover, and the first attempt showed why the id has to sit on the right node.** The thumbnail's cell and a panel share one ratio (**0.7066** against **0.7061**), so the journey is a uniform `scale` and can never be the old `scale(sx,sy)` smear. The cover rides on a `.lf-fly` layer outside the chain — outside every `overflow:hidden` face, and out of the way of a leaf's hinge matrix — and Flip matches the two nodes by a shared `data-flip-id="lfCover"`. Measured 60 ms in: the layer covers **454.5 × 643.1 px**, the thumbnail's own rect, against a **270 × 382** panel. The first build put the id on the `<img>` *inside* the layer while passing the layer as `targets`; Flip auto-assigned `auto-N`, matched nothing, and completed in **0 ms** — a failure that reads exactly like "the morph is skipped", and one that only a rect assertion at 60 ms catches, not an assertion that a tween exists.
  - **The shadow ban, measured rather than promised.** Deleted: `.lf-center-seam` (a 10 px two-sided gradient down the middle), `.lf-lift-shadow` (a 45 %-wide `blur(3px)` gradient) with its `.lf-slot.left/right` variants, `.lf-prod-panel{box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.22)}`, and `applyFlap`'s per-frame `filter:brightness()` plus generated `boxShadow` — four shadows, three of them repainted every frame on a 3D layer. What replaced them is a **1 px** crease at `rgba(25,21,16,0.15)` (`translateZ(0.6px)`), one per hinge, never animated and never a gradient, and **one** contact ellipse on the table: a flat `radial-gradient` with no `filter`, because a blurred layer inside a `preserve-3d` subtree is re-rasterised whenever anything in that subtree moves. Computed styles at all five widths: `filter: none` and `box-shadow: none` on every leaf, face, crease, the rig, the accordion and the container; the crease is `1px` of `rgba(25, 21, 16, 0.15)` — **382.094 px** tall on desktop, **300 px** wide on mobile.
  - **390 px was not a small desktop, it was broken.** The old spread stacked two pages, so at 390 px each panel was **87.75 px** inside a 124 px sheet: caption-sized type pretending to be a leaflet. Below 800 px the chain now turns on its side — `data-axis="x"`, the hinge along each leaf's top edge, `rotateX(-θ)` (negated, because CSS `rotateX` folds toward the viewer), `aspect-ratio:460/2604`, `--lf-w` capped at 300 px. Panels measure **424.56 px** tall and the strip **1698.06 px** against 4u of 1698.25 (**0.19 px**). That is taller than an 844 px room on purpose: the room scrolls and the controls go `position:sticky` at the bottom, so Fold and Unfold stay under a thumb. Back faces stay `rotateY(180deg)` on both axes because a 180° flip inverts the normal either way; the in-plane handedness differs, but at that angle only the stack's top leaf is visible and leaf 0 is pinned in front by a **−0.4 px** per-leaf z bias.
  - **Both fallbacks were measured, not assumed.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the sheet is already at **0 / 270 / 540 / 810 px** 90 ms after the click, the fly layer never shows, and no timeline is built. With `cdnjs.cloudflare.com` blocked, `window.gsap` and `window.Flip` are genuinely `false` and unfolding, folding and turning still land on exact geometry instantly — same `render()`, one pose at a time. The two CDN tags are deliberately **not** deferred: `js/main.js` runs at the end of the body and reads `window.gsap` at parse time, so a deferred GSAP would arrive after the leaflet had already chosen its no-motion path. SRI was computed from the files and cross-checked against the cdnjs API (`gsap.min.js` `sha512-oJ8QbaQT…`, `Flip.min.js` `sha512-IOMnnN/D…`).
  - **What had to keep working, and does.** `pick()` was re-pointed (`#lfBtnFold`, `#lfBtnUnfold`, `#lfBtnTurnOver`; the dead `#lfFlapL/R` and `#lfBtnClosed` are gone), so folding is still a 0.150 s flap and the folio is still a snap; the focus trap, `inert`, `aria-expanded`, `syncScrollLock()` and the Escape binding are untouched, and closing still returns focus to `#leafletThumb` with the body unlocked. No `data-magnetic` was added to anything GSAP owns. The four product faces are no longer fetched on load either: they carry `data-src` and are assigned on first open, hover or focus — roughly **270 KB** a visit that never opens the leaflet does not pay — while the four front faces stay eager, because the cover has to be decoded before Flip can measure it.
  - Harness: a new **`leaflet3d.mjs`, 87 checks, all green** — five viewports through fold → unfold → turn → close, asserting the hinge maths, the labels, zero overflow, the shadow ban, `preserve-3d`, the fly layer's rect at 60 ms, "the unfold is animated and not a jump", reduced motion, a blocked CDN, and focus return. The project's older suite had to be rewritten, not re-run: its leaflet pillar addressed `#lfShadowL`, `#lfFlapL`, `#lfPageL/R` and a 900/420 ms WAAPI pair that no longer exist, and it died on the first `getComputedStyle(null)`. Two things came out of that repair. Every motion assertion in both suites now pins `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` explicitly, because this environment's headless Chrome reports `reduce` by default — which is what made the first runs of the new suite read as "the morph is skipped" while the code was correct. And a check that asks only "is there an animation?" passes for an animation that finishes in 0 ms; the rect at 60 ms is the check that has teeth. The repaired suite now runs end to end at **168/174** — its leaflet pillar, geometry, shadow ban, morph, ARIA and close all green — and the six still failing are sound-pillar assertions written against the old static sheet, where Turn and Fold were never disabled and the room came down in one synchronous step; the wall's own snap checks go silent in the same run, which is what a modal still holding the room looks like. The audio engine itself is untouched apart from the one `pick()` line that was re-pointed.

- **The Leaflet Thumbnail Is One Cover Card, and the Morph Now Starts From Its Exact Rect** (`index.html` thumbnail CSS 238–257 + case-01 markup 882–889 — 91,945 → 92,255 B / 1,172 → 1,177 lines, LF-only, BOM-free, SHA-256 `9D43D654…`; `js/main.js` 424–461, a rename — 83,070 → 83,057 B / 1,460 lines, `7F38ED1F…`; harness 87 → **98/98** new, legacy 168/174 → **171/177**)
  - **The side-by-side preview was a spread the thumbnail could not afford.** It showed the cover *and* an interior page, which read as a spread of the finished leaflet before the visitor had asked for one — and it forced the object to be a `1fr 1fr` grid, so neither page could be the size it wanted. The interior plate, its 920×1302 load and the `.fold-shadow` conic gradient at the grid's centre are all gone: `#leafletStage .dt-wrap` count is **1**, `.fold-shadow` count is **0**, and the old `#leafletSpread` id no longer exists. What replaced the grid is `.leaflet-card` — a name that matches the object, since a single cover has no spread in it.
  - **One card, sized by width, ratio by the paper.** The stage is `min(100%, 30rem)` with `aspect-ratio: 920/1302`, and the plate is pinned to it (`height:100%`, `object-fit:cover`, a no-op at that ratio), so the attribute, the aspect-ratio box and the decoded image cannot disagree about the rect the morph will start from. Measured: **510 × 722 px** at 1440, 1024 and 768 (ratio **0.7066** at all three), **351 × 496.7** at 390 — centred in the column, with the existing CTA 34 px below it and also centred.
  - **The Flip id stayed on the cover, and the journey got shorter and cleaner.** `data-flip-id="lfCover"` is still on the single `<img>`, which is still the node `leafletThumb.querySelector('[data-flip-id]')` resolves to, so `Flip.from(Flip.getState(thumbCover), {targets: lfFly, scale:true})` needed no change. The payoff is measurable: the fly layer's rect at 60 ms is now **510 × 722 against the thumbnail's 510 × 722** (it was 454.5 × 643.1 and still is not a smear) and the card shares **0.7066** with the **270 × 382** panel, so the whole journey is one uniform scale of **0.529**. The old grid's `gap:3rem` (51 px) is no longer a number the morph has to survive.
  - **The perspective followed the card instead of the spread.** 1400 px against a 960 px stage was a 1.46:1 depth; the card is 510 px, so it is now `perspective:calc(var(--lf-thumb-w) * 1.46)` — **744.6 px**, the same depth at full size, a little flatter where a narrow screen caps the card. The sheen `::after` is `inset:0` on the stage, and the stage *is* the card, so the highlight now covers exactly the paper instead of 960 px of column with a 510 px card in the middle of it.
  - **What the tilt lost, and did not.** `#leafletSpread` became `#leafletCard` (3 renamed selectors, 5 references in `main.js`); the pointer maths, the `MAX_TILT` of 6°, the `--gx/--gy` sheen tracking and the CSS spring are byte-for-byte the same. Verified on the card: `rotateX(3.6deg) rotateY(4.2deg) translateZ(0px)` on pointermove, `''` after pointerleave, and under reduced motion `''` with `transitionDuration: 0s`. Also deleted: `.case-01 .leaflet-spread` from the ≤800 px single-column list, and `.case-01 .fold-shadow{display:none}` — a rule whose entire job was hiding a crease that no longer exists.
  - **The suites were updated where they described the layout, not where they described behaviour.** `verify.mjs` read `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.fold-shadow')).display` in its viewport matrix — a dead field nothing consumed, and a hard crash once the node was gone — and drove the tilt through `#leafletSpread`; both now address `.leaflet-card`, and the dead field became a real assertion (*one plate, no crease, ratio 0.7066* at 1024 / 768 / 390). The new suite gained **11 checks**: per-width page count, ratio, plate fill, stage-equals-card, the 1.46 depth, and the id shared with the fly layer at 390 and 1440, plus the tilt round trip. Legacy went 168/174 → **171/177** with the same six pre-existing sound-pillar failures and nothing new. One loose end, left deliberately: `images/leaflet-inner-thumb.webp` (**154,772 B**) is now referenced by nothing and is still in the tree — deleting an asset is its own decision, not this one.



- **Step 5 — One Asterisk, the Verse as Typography, and a Travertine Room with a Guestbook in It** (`index.html` §04 reticle, §11 footer, §12 the room, §12d register, §13 responsive — 76,301 → 87,642 B / 970 → 1,118 lines, LF-only, BOM-free, SHA-256 `37DA65C8…`; `js/main.js` 76,020 → 78,075 B / 1,333 → 1,361 lines, `6BD3A045…`; `js/ledger.js` new, 15,983 B / 328 lines, `8F4AF5F2…`; harness 150 → 173/173)

  - **Schema, because there is no migration runner here.** The DDL lives in this entry so the project is reproducible from the repository:
    ```sql
    create table if not exists public.ledger (
      id         uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
      name       text not null check (char_length(name) between 1 and 40),
      note       text not null check (char_length(note) between 3 and 240),
      approved   boolean not null default true,
      created_at timestamptz not null default now()
    );
    alter table public.ledger enable row level security;
    create policy "ledger is public to read" on public.ledger for select using (approved = true);
    create policy "anyone may sign once"     on public.ledger for insert with check (approved = true);
    alter table public.ledger replica identity full;   -- the INSERT payload carries the row, not an id
    -- plus publication membership for supabase_realtime, and an index on created_at
    ```
    The publishable key can select approved rows and insert one; it cannot read an unapproved row, update, or delete. The 40/240 limits are enforced twice — in the client so a visitor gets a sentence instead of a 400, and in the table so the client cannot be the only enforcement.

Two voices: **click** = band-passed noise transient (0.062 s) over a triangle drop from 150/190 Hz to 70 Hz (0.062 s — the weight a switch has and a burst of highs does not); **rustle** = pink noise through a swept band-pass (0.9 → 2.4 kHz on open, the reverse on close), a 2.6 kHz low-pass to keep it acoustic, and a 7–10 Hz amplitude flutter because paper arrives in catches rather than as one smooth hiss — 1.26 s to open, 0.96 s to close, 0.7 s for a link, panned randomly ±0.35.
  - **The context is a gesture, not a page load.** Zero `AudioContext` constructed on load; exactly one on the first real press; state `running`; and one 1-sample buffer is started *inside* that gesture, which is what Safari needs before it will output anything at all. `arm()` is idempotent and doubles as the resume path, so the same call serves the first press and every return from a hidden tab.
  - **What makes which noise.** One delegated table on capture-phase `pointerdown` (the press itself, before anything can navigate away) plus `click` with `detail === 0` for keyboard and assistive tech — which never produce a pointerdown and must not be the one silent path into the site. Nav press = soft click, any other control = full click, leaflet thumb / open button = paper opening, flap + turn-over = a turn, close + panels-closed = paper closing, `.mag-link` = a short rustle, the comparison grab = one soft click per press. Prose is silent (0 nodes scheduled, asserted), the toggle confirms itself and is excluded from the delegate, `[disabled]` stays silent, and hover/focus/scroll say nothing at all — unprompted sound is what people file as a bug.
  - **Rate limits and a ceiling.** 40 ms between clicks, 220 ms between rustles, four concurrent voices, and every voice releases from *both* the terminal node's `onended` and a timer, so a context that never resumes cannot park the counter at the ceiling. A voice that throws resets the counter through `guard()` instead of slowly silting it up — the press it was decorating still goes through.
  - **Mute is one state behind three mirrors**: `aria-pressed`, `documentElement.dataset.sound`, and `localStorage['ad-sound']`, with the bus gain closed by `setTargetAtTime` so it cannot thump (the press that mutes is still heard: 0.9 → 0 over ~45 ms, and the click is 62 ms long). Asserted end to end: toggle → `false`/`off`/`off` → later presses schedule nothing → reload keeps it (`0` contexts, still `off`) → switching back on re-arms exactly one context and clears storage. With no Web Audio the control hides rather than lying; without JS the `<noscript>` block hides it.

The mark is now crisp at any DPI/zoom, inherits the headline's Cormorant Garamond 700 weight and `--bone` colour, and scales with `--mag-name-size` through `em` with no HTTP request.
  - The markup was already clean text (`VISION<span class="mag-asterisk">*</span>`), so no HTML change was needed; the only text-suppression trick was the removed `color:transparent`.
  - Chose ASCII `*` (U+002A) over the Dingbats starbursts `✻` (U+273B) / `✳` (U+2733) / `✽` (U+273D). Headless-canvas probe on the loaded webfont: `*` advances 44.8px at 100px in Cormorant Garamond vs 50px in the generic serif fallback (proving the family was genuinely loaded and rendering its own glyph), while all three Dingbats codepoints measure an identical 88.82px under both Cormorant and the generic serif — Cormorant Garamond contains no Dingbats glyphs, so those characters would silently render in a system symbol font (Segoe UI Symbol / Apple Symbols / DejaVu), losing the masthead's weight, contrast and cross-platform consistency.
  - Footer trigger converted from raster to text: `<img class="trigger-asterisk-img" src="images/asterisk.png" alt="*">` → `<span class="trigger-asterisk">*</span>` with `.trigger-asterisk{font-family:var(--serif);font-weight:700;font-size:1.1rem;line-height:1;color:rgba(237,230,212,0.55);transition:color 0.25s}` and hover `rgba(237,230,212,0.95)`. Left as real text rather than `aria-hidden` so the button's accessible name still contains "asterisk", matching the previous `alt="*"` behaviour.
  - Favicon converted from PNG to an inline SVG data URI (6-spoke bone asterisk on ink, `rx=10`), following the file's existing inline-SVG data-URI convention. No raster reference remains anywhere in the document; `images/asterisk.png` is now an orphaned asset (left on disk — this machine has no `git`, so deletions are irreversible).
  - Caveat: older Safari versions ignore `data:image/svg+xml` favicons; Chromium, Firefox and current Safari render them.

## [2026-10-16]
- **Fixed Eid Al Adha Case Study Structure**: Extracted `.case-04` (Eid Al Adha) from inside the `.case-03` container in `index.html`. Updated section numbering.
- **Improved Conference Room Installation Wall**:
  - Refined `.wall-row` CSS: added `gap: 2.5rem` and `padding` for better desktop spacing.
  - Updated `.frame` CSS: added `z-index` and `margin-bottom` to prevent overlap.
  - Refined `.frame-label` CSS: improved readability, positioning, and set `pointer-events: none`.
- **Enhanced Leaflet Modal (.lf-modal) for Desktop**:
  - Updated CSS for `max-width: 1100px` and adjusted padding/column proportions in `.leaflet-spread` for a better editorial layout on large screens.
- **Corrected Header Asterisk (.mag-asterisk) Rendering** (supersedes the earlier `16px x 16px` / `font-size: 0` entry for this rule):
  - Root cause of the invisible mark: the previous rule pinned a fixed `16px x 16px` box and set `font-size: 0`, which collapsed the `em`-based sizing to `0x0`, so neither the mask nor the background could paint. Do not reintroduce `font-size: 0` here.
  - Sizing is now `width: 0.4455em; height: 0.30em` — the exact 300:202 ratio of `images/asterisk.png` — so the mark scales with `--mag-name-size` (49.23 x 33.15px at 1920px).
  - Base rule paints the inverted raster glyph (`background: url('images/asterisk.png') center/contain no-repeat` + `filter: invert(1)`); a `@supports (mask: url(...))` branch repaints it as a bone-coloured CSS mask for engines with mask support.
  - Verified by pixel-classification screenshots served over `http://` with no browser flags: the masked branch paints 579px of bone inside a 49x33 box at the real 1920 name size, and the fallback branch paints the identical glyph as an inverted raster.
- **Made the Eid Al Adha Mandala Reveal CSS-Native (fail-open)**: `.eid-reveal` is visible by default (`clip-path: circle(75% at 50% 50%)`) and animates only where `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` exists. Removed the now-dead JS `IntersectionObserver` gate in `main.js` — it observed the element that was itself clipped to `circle(0%)`, so its callback never fired and `#eidImg` stayed permanently invisible.
- **Documented the Masked Title Reveal Contract**: `.mask-wrap` / `.stat-snap` elements stay hidden (`translateY(110%)`) until the single sitewide `IntersectionObserver` in `main.js` adds `.vis`. This is intentional on-scroll behaviour — title content is legitimately absent from pre-scroll screenshots.

- **Fixed Structural Numbering/Nesting Errors**: Renumbered 'Did You Know?' case to 05 and 'Sales Operations' case to 06, fixing invalid/duplicated class definitions and ensuring consistent section indexing across the portfolio.
